findings: Block key parsing fragility — computeBestTimeAnalysis assumes all block keys follow HH:mm format. Malformed keys fail silently (isNaN check), potentially skewing peak hour analysis.

Churn risk threshold conflict — Plan specifies >7 days triggers alert; implementation uses >7 in condition, creating asymmetry (8 days triggers alert, 7 days doesn't). Alert text says 'for X days' which is technically accurate but the integer boundary should be clarified.
Missing data quality gate — Plan calls for 'placeholder data if <14 days of history,' but implementation has no check. New users see accurate-but-sparse 30-day trends instead of placeholder message.
Hourly distribution rendering limitation — 6-column grid (24 hours ÷ 4 rows) compresses on mobile. Heatmap may become difficult to read on narrow screens.
